# Boatwright in Residence Apprenticeship Program

![Blanchard Junior Knockabout sailboat under restoration](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1617146515411-7J35PARVP8R67WP1G4GP/Blanchard.jpg)

The Boatwright in Residence Apprenticeship Program is aimed at recent graduates of wooden boatbuilding programs, offering a chance to build skills and network with the local industry.

## 2021 Program

Apprentices worked on restoring *Pamela*, a 21-foot Blanchard Jr Knockabout built in 1936: replacing planking, re-bedding the keel, replacing floor timbers, installing steam-bent white oak frames, and building a new mast. The restoration began in 2019 with funding from King County's [4Culture](https://www.4culture.org) and involved apprentices from Gibson EK high school.

![A volunteer works on the bottom planking of a boat](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1617147023596-4MJHYL8UPCCWPFKNMFJV/Hvalsoe.jpg)

## Facilities

CWB has four fully outfitted boatshops. The 1,000 square foot Bill Garden Boatshop opened in 2018 in the Wagner Education Center.

## Leadership

Apprentices work under Josh Anderson, Executive Director, and Dustin Espey, Livery Manager.

## Funding

The program is supported by the RPM Foundation ([www.rpm.foundation](http://www.rpm.foundation/)), an educational grant-making program of America's Automotive Trust.

## Apply

The 2026 application process is open. Inquiries: [hiring@cwb.org](mailto:hiring@cwb.org). See [detailed application information here](https://www.cwb.org/s/BoatwrightinResidence.pdf).
